items.title: Amaara
items.caption: A two-piece traditional bridal look in handwoven cotton-silk. The structured bodice is boned and hand-felled, the wrapper cut on a soft bias so it falls without clinging. Worn with a gele drafted to the same head-turn.

items.title: Serwaa
items.caption: Kente-paneled shirt dress with a shirtwaist sleeve. The kente is cut on the bias and panel-set by hand so the pattern reads across the body rather than down it. Finished with corozo buttons and a split hem.

items.title: Nhyira
items.caption: Six metres of silk mikado, drafted into a cathedral train with a hand-corded bodice. The shoulder is built on a floating foundation so the line stays clean under a veil. Built over nine weeks, worn once.

items.title: Aylin
items.caption: An asymmetric evening gown in crepe, with a single draped panel falling from the left shoulder. Fully lined, invisible side zip, weighted hem so it moves as one piece of cloth.

items.title: Efua
items.caption: A power suit drafted properly — not shrunk from a menswear block. Single-button jacket, hand-padded shoulder, trousers blocked to a full break. The jacket is lined in a vintage print chosen by the client.

items.title: Maame Gyanwaa
items.caption: The dress we are asked for most. A clean slip in cotton voile with a removable belt, drafted with enough ease to sit down in. Four lengths in production, all made to measure.

items.title: Adwoa
items.caption: A cathedral veil in silk tulle, cut long enough to trail a step behind and hemmed by hand so it never frays against the floor. Worn open, so the setting reads behind the line of the shoulder rather than through the cloth.

items.title: Akosua
items.caption: The gown we are asked for when there is architecture to work with. Silk mikado through the body, a chapel train drafted in one piece, and a bodice corseted to the wearer rather than to a standard size.
items.fabric: Silk mikado, cotton coutil, bone corset

items.title: Abena
items.caption: Single button, hand-padded shoulder, trousers blocked to a full break. Cut long enough in the jacket to close over a dress, which is the only thing that makes a suit worth owning twice.

items.title: Yaa
items.caption: Black crepe, cut on the bias and left unlined through the skirt so it falls from the hip. One seam at the waist and nothing else — the cloth is left to do the rest of the work.

items.title: Zuri
items.caption: The shirt dress, made properly. Long sleeve, a cuff that closes without a gap, and a hem drafted to sit below the knee on a tall frame. Washed cotton, so it can be worn hard and washed often.

items.title: Naa Dedei
items.caption: Kente cut for the body rather than laid on it, with the panel joins matched across the shoulder by eye. A gele drafted to the same head-turn, wrapped on the morning itself.

items.title: Amma
items.caption: A slip in silk crepe with a gold chain at the neck — the only jewellery we ever add ourselves. Drafted close, weighted at the hem, and finished by hand at the strap.
